title: Travel & Transport
subtitle: Take trains, catch flights, and hit the road in French

lessons.title: À la gare
lessons.description: Buy train tickets, read schedules, and find your platform with confidence.

blocks.heading: Buying a train ticket
blocks.body: At the station, you buy your ticket at "le guichet" (the ticket window) or at a machine. The two key words are "un aller simple" (a one-way ticket) and "un aller-retour" (a round trip). Add your destination with "pour" and you are ready to travel.

examples.french: Je voudrais un aller-retour pour Lyon, s'il vous plaît.
examples.english: I would like a round-trip ticket to Lyon, please.

examples.french: Un aller simple en seconde classe, s'il vous plaît.
examples.english: A one-way ticket in second class, please.

examples.french: À quelle heure part le prochain train pour Paris ?
examples.english: What time does the next train to Paris leave?

examples.french: C'est direct ou il y a une correspondance ?
examples.english: Is it direct or is there a connection?

examples.french: Le billet coûte quarante-cinq euros.
examples.english: The ticket costs forty-five euros.

blocks.tip: With a paper ticket, remember to "composter" (validate) it in the yellow machine before boarding — an unvalidated ticket can mean a fine.

blocks.heading: Reading the departure board
blocks.body: The board shows "le départ" (departure), "l'arrivée" (arrival), and "la voie" or "le quai" (the track / platform). "En retard" means delayed, and "à l'heure" means on time. Trains in France run on the 24-hour clock.

examples.french: Le train pour Marseille part de la voie huit.
examples.english: The train to Marseille leaves from track eight.

examples.french: Le TGV de dix heures a vingt minutes de retard.
examples.english: The 10 o'clock TGV is twenty minutes late.

examples.french: L'arrivée est prévue à dix-huit heures trente.
examples.english: The arrival is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

examples.french: Le départ est à quinze heures dix, quai deux.
examples.english: The departure is at 3:10 p.m., platform two.

examples.french: Regarde l'horaire sur le panneau !
examples.english: Look at the schedule on the board!

blocks.tip: "Le TGV" (train à grande vitesse) is France's high-speed train — Paris to Lyon takes only two hours.

blocks.heading: On the train
blocks.body: Once aboard, find your "place" (seat) in the right "wagon" (carriage). "Le contrôleur" (the ticket inspector) may check your ticket during the trip. If you miss a train or a connection, use the verb "rater".

blocks.heading: Prendre — the essential travel verb
blocks.body: "Prendre" (to take) is irregular: je prends, tu prends, il/elle prend, nous prenons, vous prenez, ils/elles prennent. You use it for every kind of transport: prendre le train, le bus, l'avion, le métro. In the passé composé it becomes "j'ai pris".

examples.french: Je prends le train tous les matins.
examples.english: I take the train every morning.

examples.french: Nous prenons le TGV de huit heures.
examples.english: We are taking the eight o'clock TGV.

examples.french: Ils prennent souvent le métro.
examples.english: They often take the metro.

examples.french: Hier, j'ai pris un taxi pour aller à la gare.
examples.english: Yesterday, I took a taxi to go to the station.

examples.french: Tu as pris tes billets ?
examples.english: Did you get your tickets?

blocks.tip: The "d" is silent in the singular: "prend" sounds like "prahn". In "prennent", you hear the double n: "prenn".

items.tip: "Aller" is ah-LAY — the two l's sound like a single l, and "simple" ends in a soft "pluh".

passages.title: Au guichet de la gare de Lyon
passages.french:
— Bonjour, je voudrais un billet pour Marseille, s'il vous plaît.
— Bien sûr. Un aller simple ou un aller-retour ?
— Un aller-retour, en seconde classe.
— Vous partez quand ?
— Demain matin, vers neuf heures.
— Il y a un TGV direct à neuf heures quinze. Le retour est valable un mois.
— Parfait. Le trajet dure combien de temps ?
— Trois heures dix. Ça fait quatre-vingt-deux euros.
— Très bien. Le train part de quelle voie ?
— Regardez le panneau le jour du départ, madame.
passages.english:
— Hello, I would like a ticket to Marseille, please.
— Of course. One-way or round trip?
— A round trip, in second class.
— When are you leaving?
— Tomorrow morning, around nine o'clock.
— There is a direct TGV at 9:15. The return is valid for one month.
— Perfect. How long does the journey take?
— Three hours and ten minutes. That comes to eighty-two euros.
— Very good. Which track does the train leave from?
— Check the board on the day of departure, ma'am.

lessons.title: À l'aéroport et à l'hôtel
lessons.description: Check in for a flight, get through the airport, and book a hotel room.

blocks.heading: At the check-in desk
blocks.body: At the airport, you first "enregistrer" (check in) your "bagages" (luggage) and receive your "carte d'embarquement" (boarding pass). Keep your "passeport" ready for "le contrôle" (security and passport control).

examples.french: Je voudrais enregistrer cette valise, s'il vous plaît.
examples.english: I would like to check this suitcase, please.

examples.french: Voici mon passeport et ma carte d'embarquement.
examples.english: Here is my passport and my boarding pass.

examples.french: Vous avez un bagage à main ?
examples.english: Do you have a carry-on bag?

examples.french: L'embarquement commence à dix heures vingt.
examples.english: Boarding starts at 10:20.

examples.french: Le vol AF 1234 part de la porte B12.
examples.english: Flight AF 1234 leaves from gate B12.

blocks.tip: In French airports, "la porte" is the gate. Listen for "embarquement immédiat" — it means boarding now, hurry!

blocks.heading: On the plane
blocks.body: The plane "décolle" (takes off) and "atterrit" (lands). The crew — "l'hôtesse de l'air" and "le steward" — ask you to fasten "votre ceinture" (your seatbelt). "Le vol" is the flight itself.

examples.french: L'avion décolle dans vingt minutes.
examples.english: The plane takes off in twenty minutes.

examples.french: Attachez votre ceinture, s'il vous plaît.
examples.english: Fasten your seatbelt, please.

examples.french: Le vol dure une heure et demie.
examples.english: The flight lasts an hour and a half.

examples.french: Nous atterrissons à Nice à quatorze heures.
examples.english: We land in Nice at 2 p.m.

examples.french: Mon vol a été annulé à cause de la neige.
examples.english: My flight was cancelled because of the snow.

blocks.heading: Booking and checking in at the hotel
blocks.body: At the hotel, you talk to "la réception". Ask for "une chambre simple" (a single room) or "une chambre double" (a double room), say how many "nuits" (nights) you are staying, and ask if breakfast is "compris" (included).

examples.french: J'ai réservé une chambre double pour deux nuits.
examples.english: I booked a double room for two nights.

examples.french: Le petit-déjeuner est compris ?
examples.english: Is breakfast included?

examples.french: Votre chambre est au troisième étage.
examples.english: Your room is on the third floor.

examples.french: Voici votre clé. L'ascenseur est à droite.
examples.english: Here is your key. The elevator is on the right.

examples.french: Désolé, l'hôtel est complet ce week-end.
examples.english: Sorry, the hotel is full this weekend.

examples.french: Le wifi est gratuit dans toutes les chambres.
examples.english: The wifi is free in all the rooms.

blocks.tip: In France, the ground floor is "le rez-de-chaussée" — so "le premier étage" is one floor up (the American second floor).

blocks.heading: Talking about travel plans: le futur proche
blocks.body: To talk about plans, French uses "aller" + infinitive: "je vais partir" (I am going to leave). It is the easiest future tense — just conjugate "aller" (je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont) and add the verb.

examples.french: Je vais prendre l'avion demain.
examples.english: I am going to take the plane tomorrow.

examples.french: Nous allons réserver un hôtel à Nice.
examples.english: We are going to book a hotel in Nice.

examples.french: Le vol va décoller dans dix minutes.
examples.english: The flight is going to take off in ten minutes.

examples.french: Tu vas enregistrer ta valise ?
examples.english: Are you going to check in your suitcase?

examples.french: Ils vont passer une semaine à Paris.
examples.english: They are going to spend a week in Paris.

blocks.tip: For the negative, wrap ne...pas around "aller": "Je ne vais pas annuler mon voyage."

passages.title: À la réception de l'hôtel
passages.french:
— Bonsoir, j'ai une réservation au nom de Dubois.
— Bonsoir, madame. Oui, une chambre double pour trois nuits.

— Parfait. Il y a le wifi dans la chambre ?
— Oui, il est gratuit. Voici votre clé, chambre 24, au deuxième étage.
— Merci. L'ascenseur est où ?
— Au fond du couloir, à gauche. Bonne soirée, madame !
passages.english:
— Good evening, I have a reservation under the name Dubois.
— Good evening, ma'am. Yes, a double room for three nights.
— That's right. Is breakfast included?
— Yes, it is served from seven to ten.
— Perfect. Is there wifi in the room?
— Yes, it's free. Here is your key, room 24, on the second floor.
— Thank you. Where is the elevator?
— At the end of the hallway, on the left. Have a good evening, ma'am!

lessons.title: En route !
lessons.description: Rent a car, find your way on the road, and replace places and quantities with y and en.

blocks.heading: Renting a car
blocks.body: At the rental desk you will need three sentences: what you want, for how long, and what is included. Prices are given "par jour" (per day) and the agent will ask for your "permis de conduire".

examples.french: Je voudrais louer une petite voiture pour trois jours.
examples.english: I'd like to rent a small car for three days.

examples.french: Voici mon permis de conduire.
examples.english: Here is my driving licence.

examples.french: L'assurance est comprise dans le prix ?
examples.english: Is insurance included in the price?

examples.french: Il faut rendre la voiture avec le plein.
examples.english: You have to return the car with a full tank.

examples.french: C'est combien par jour ?
examples.english: How much is it per day?

blocks.tip: In France a rental car is usually "une boîte manuelle" (manual). Ask for "une boîte automatique" if you need one.

blocks.heading: On the road
blocks.body: French motorways (les autoroutes) are fast but you pay at a "péage". Speed limits are shown on round signs: 130 on the motorway, 80 or 90 on country roads, 50 in town. Stop at a "station-service" to fill up.

examples.french: Nous avons pris l'autoroute A7 vers Marseille.
examples.english: We took the A7 motorway towards Marseille.

examples.french: On s'arrête à la prochaine station-service ?
examples.english: Shall we stop at the next petrol station?

examples.french: Le plein, s'il vous plaît.
examples.english: Fill it up, please.

examples.french: Attention, il y a un radar après le péage.
examples.english: Careful, there's a speed camera after the toll.

examples.french: Ralentis, la limitation est à cinquante.
examples.english: Slow down, the limit is fifty.

blocks.heading: Asking the way again
blocks.body: Directions come back constantly on a road trip. Keep these ready: "Pardon, je cherche...", "C'est loin ?", "On continue tout droit ?". The answers use tournez, continuez, prenez and traversez.

examples.french: Pardon, je cherche la route de Nîmes.
examples.english: Excuse me, I'm looking for the road to Nîmes.

examples.french: Continuez tout droit jusqu'au rond-point.
examples.english: Carry straight on to the roundabout.

examples.french: Au carrefour, tournez à gauche.
examples.english: At the crossroads, turn left.

examples.french: Prenez la deuxième sortie du rond-point.
examples.english: Take the second exit at the roundabout.

blocks.heading: The pronoun y = there
blocks.body: "Y" replaces a place already mentioned, usually introduced by à, en, dans, sur or chez. It goes directly before the verb: J'y vais. In the passé composé it sits before the helper: J'y suis allé. With two verbs it goes before the infinitive: Je vais y aller.

examples.french: Tu vas à Bordeaux ? — Oui, j'y vais demain.
examples.english: Are you going to Bordeaux? — Yes, I'm going there tomorrow.

examples.french: Nous y sommes restés trois jours.
examples.english: We stayed there for three days.

examples.french: On y va !
examples.english: Let's go!

examples.french: Je n'y suis jamais allé.
examples.english: I have never been there.

examples.french: Elle veut y retourner cet été.
examples.english: She wants to go back there this summer.

blocks.tip: "Y" also replaces à + a thing: Tu penses à la réservation ? — Oui, j'y pense.

blocks.heading: The pronoun en = some / of it / of them
blocks.body: "En" replaces du / de la / des / de + noun, and any quantity. Same position as y: before the verb, or before the helper in the past. Keep the number or quantity word at the end: J'en ai deux.

examples.french: Tu as de l'essence ? — Oui, j'en ai.
examples.english: Do you have petrol? — Yes, I have some.

examples.french: Des cartes routières ? Nous en avons acheté deux.
examples.english: Road maps? We bought two of them.

examples.french: Il n'y a plus de péages ? — Non, il n'y en a plus.
examples.english: Are there no more tolls? — No, there aren't any more.

examples.french: Elle revient de Nice. — Elle en revient ce soir.
examples.english: She's coming back from Nice. — She's coming back from there tonight.

examples.french: Combien de kilomètres ? — On en a fait cinq cents.
examples.english: How many kilometres? — We did five hundred of them.

blocks.tip: Quick rule: à → y, de → en. Learn them as a pair and half the difficulty disappears.

passages.title: Sur la route des vacances
passages.french:
Samedi, nous avons loué une voiture à l'agence de la gare.
L'employé a regardé mon permis de conduire et nous a donné les clés.
D'abord, nous avons mis les valises dans le coffre et nous avons attaché nos ceintures.
Nous sommes partis vers huit heures pour éviter les embouteillages.
Sur l'autoroute, nous avons roulé pendant deux heures, puis nous nous sommes arrêtés à une station-service.
J'ai fait le plein et Julie a acheté des sandwichs : elle en a pris quatre !
Après le péage, le GPS a proposé un autre itinéraire par la petite route.
Nous y sommes allés et le paysage était magnifique.
Enfin, nous sommes arrivés au village à midi et nous nous sommes garés devant l'hôtel.
passages.english:
On Saturday, we rented a car at the agency by the station.
The employee looked at my driving licence and gave us the keys.
First, we put the suitcases in the boot and fastened our seat belts.
We left around eight to avoid the traffic jams.
On the motorway, we drove for two hours, then we stopped at a petrol station.
I filled up the tank and Julie bought some sandwiches: she took four of them!
After the toll, the GPS suggested another route along the small road.
We went there and the scenery was magnificent.
Finally, we arrived at the village at noon and parked in front of the hotel.
